subject: Post-demo security intake — SOC2 Type II, temporary attestation & portal access (Medisolutions)
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan@redwood.com>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@medisolutions.com>, procurement@medisolutions.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Jul 2028 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo security intake — SOC2 Type II, temporary attestation & portal access (Medisolutions)

Hi Alex / procurement team — thanks again for taking the demo today. Quick recap and next steps from our side so procurement/security can kick off the intake: 

- You asked for our most recent SOC 2 Type II report (if available), a short bridge/summary, and a temporary attestation while the full report is processed. I attached a one-page SOC2 summary and a temporary attestation template for your intake.
- We can provision access to our trust portal (read-only) for your security reviewers — typically we invite one or two reviewers and grant view-only rights to report artifacts and evidence indexes.
- If you have a vendor security questionnaire (VSQ) or procurement intake form, please share the link or DocuSign envelope and we’ll respond.

Action items I propose: 
1) Alex / procurement: share the VSQ link or preferred intake process and the person who will own evidence review.
2) Jordan (me): upload the SOC2 one-pager and temporary attestation to our trust portal; notify you when invite is sent.
3) Marissa: if the full Type II is available from our auditor, pls attach or call out redactions.
4) Ben: prepare any contract/PO guidance for procurement (pricing/term notes).

Attachments: Redwood_SOC2_TypeII_summary.pdf (summary), Temporary_Attestation_Template.docx (editable).

Thanks — happy to hop on a short call if you'd like to review details.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
jordan@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0192

--
Redwood Inference — production-first LLM inference runtime.

Thanks Jordan — appreciated the recap and the attachments. A few things from our side: 

- Procurement owns the intake; I’ve looped them on this thread. For the VSQ, we use a short questionnaire hosted in SharePoint — procurement will send the link.
- Our security reviewers will need confirmation of data residency and whether Redwood processes EEA data or PHI (HIPAA). Please state whether you consider any of your hosted features to be HIPAA-handled or suitable for PHI processing.
- For now we usually accept a temporary attestation for the security procurement bucket while the full Type II is requested; please include expected timing for the auditor report if available.

Marissa / Jordan / Ben — thanks for the quick coordination. We’ve provisioned a reviewer seat for Claire Lee and a backup (procurement@medisolutions.com) in your trust portal; invite link: https://trust.redwood.com/invite/medisolutions-AB12CD. 

Portal notes: reviewers will receive read-only access to artifact metadata and the auditor-delivered report (where permitted). Please confirm whether the full Type II will be uploaded or if we should expect a redacted version + temporary attestation. Also confirm whether Redwood allows viewer access scoped to named individuals (yes) or by service account (no).

On PHI/EEA: at this stage we are not processing PHI, but we reserve the right to escalate to HIPAA requirements if the scope of integration changes. Please indicate in the attestation whether Redwood supports HIPAA BAAs (yes/no) and the current stance on EEA data residency.

Procurement requests a signed attestation (DocuSign) while we wait for the full Type II. If you send the DocuSign envelope link we’ll get it routed to our legal promptly.
